gaps.sentence: In Sweden the shops close early, ___ in Spain they stay open until ten.
gaps.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts parallel facts about two countries.

gaps.sentence: I enjoyed the film; the ending was weak, ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Though' can come at the end of a sentence as a casual contrast marker; the others cannot.

gaps.sentence: ___ did he apologise, but he also refunded the full amount.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only did he..., but he also...' is the correlative pattern with inversion.

gaps.sentence: The expedition will go ahead ___ the sponsors confirm the funding.
gaps.explanation: 'Provided that' = only if, a formal positive condition.

gaps.sentence: The essay was submitted late and, ___, it ignored the brief entirely.
gaps.explanation: 'What is more' adds a further, stronger point to an already negative picture.

gaps.sentence: ___ fast you run, the train won't wait for you.
He had hardly stepped off the plane ___ he was rushed into a meeting.
He spends money ___ it grew on trees.
gaps.explanation: 'As if it grew on trees' — the unreal comparison justifies the criticism.
